pergunta: Can a tank with neither the best armor nor the best gun be the right piece?
resumo: M4 Sherman with the 75 mm gun: specs, strengths, its reputation for burning and the battles it fought in, from El Alamein to Montese. All sourced.
abertura: The M4 Sherman was the medium tank of the United States and of a good part of the Allies from 1942 on. This page covers the first versions, the M4 and the M4A1, with the 75 mm gun.

Steven Zaloga, the historian who has written most about it, admits that the Sherman had neither the best armor nor the best gun. The American bet was a different one: a very reliable tank, cheap to build, in quantity. The specs below show what that bet bought and what it cost.

paragrafos: The Sherman was the general-purpose medium tank: accompanying the infantry, breaking through positions and exploiting the breakthrough. According to Steven Zaloga, the United States chose to concentrate on a tank that was very reliable and relatively cheap to build; from the point of view of those in command, he says, it was an excellent weapon.

It debuted with the British 8th Army at the second battle of El Alamein, in October 1942, with 252 tanks ready. The site Tank Archives, based on Pier Paolo Battistelli, puts the first action at dawn on 24 October.

It worked. The Tank Museum sums up the Shermans as reliable, durable and easy to maintain, and records that the parts, made by hundreds of factories, were fully interchangeable, a rare thing among the tanks of the war.

In 1942, the gun was a strength too. For the Tank Museum, at the end of that year the 75 mm was as good as the gun of most tanks, or better, and its high-explosive shell was more powerful than those of the guns that came later. Most of a tank's targets are not another tank.

There is a counterpoint from the period. A British report from the desert, summarized by Tank Archives, complained about the reliability of the engines and about the rubber on the tracks, which came off after 600 miles.
The armor and the gun fell behind when the Tiger and the Panther appeared. Zaloga does not hide it: the Sherman had neither the best armor nor the best gun.

And there was fire. In a US Army study of 1945, cited by the Tank Museum and by Zaloga, 60% to 80% of the first Shermans burned when the armor was penetrated. The main cause, for Zaloga, for the Tank Museum and for the British report of 1942, was the ammunition stowed in the hull sides, not the gasoline.

The remedy came in two stages. First, plates welded on the outside, over the ammunition racks. Then, in the new tanks, the ammunition moved to liquid-filled bins in the floor, and the proportion of those that burned fell to 10% to 15%, in the same study. Every 75 mm M4 was built with the old arrangement.

The Brazilian Expeditionary Force had no tanks of its own. The magazine of the Army's Armor Instruction Center records that the reconnaissance squadron, with M8 cars, was the only Brazilian unit to use armor in the war.

The medium tanks that appear alongside the Brazilians were American. A paper from the Agulhas Negras Military Academy, based on Captain Plínio Pitaluga's report, records a platoon of American medium tanks in the consolidation of the capture of Montese. Which unit they came from, the open sources do not allow us to say.

batalhas.texto: Among the 8th Army's more than a thousand tanks in October 1942 were the first American Shermans, sent after the fall of Tobruk. The British had about 2 to 1 in men and in tanks.

According to the English Wikipedia, the Brazilian infantry advanced on 14 April 1945 with M8 armored cars and Sherman tanks. The advance, fast and with armor, led the German command to treat Montese as a possible real Allied objective in the sector.

In the early evening of 20 September 1944, Guards tanks crossed the Nijmegen road bridge, and on the other side they stopped for about 18 hours. The photo on the page shows a Sherman on the bridge. Ahead lay 11 km of road raised above the polder, which the commander of the Guards Armoured Division described as the most unsuitable terrain for tanks that could be imagined.

In the third assault, in March 1944, the tanks ran into the craters of the bombing that flattened the town. A color photograph of 18 May 1944 shows a destroyed Sherman beside a Bailey bridge, in the ruins of Cassino.

veredito: On the board, the Sherman is the pawn that arrives in numbers. Piece for piece, it lost to the best German pieces from 1943 on. But it arrived in working order, with spare parts, on any front, and it was replaced when lost.

It is a planning choice, not an accident: trading the best possible tank for many tanks that were good enough. The cost of that choice shows in the proportion of those that burned, and it was paid by the crews.

mitos.circula: The Sherman caught fire because its engine ran on gasoline.
mitos.registro: The main cause was the ammunition in the hull sides, according to Steven Zaloga, the Tank Museum and a British report of 1942. Zaloga points out that the German tanks also ran on gasoline.

mitos.circula: The soldiers called it the Ronson because of the lighter's slogan, that it always lit first time.
mitos.registro: The site Tank and AFV News looked for the Ronson advertisements and did not find the slogan in any from the period immediately before the war or from the war itself; the closest one is from 1929. The nickname could well have existed; the explanation by the slogan does not hold up in the advertisements.

mitos.circula: It took five Shermans to destroy one Tiger.
mitos.registro: Steven Zaloga, in a 2015 interview, calls the story totally apocryphal. No source from the period was found for the ratio.

perguntas.p: How many Sherman tanks were built?
perguntas.r: 49,234 in the English Wikipedia table, attributed to Steven Zaloga; the text of the same article gives 49,324. Of the first 75 mm versions, there were 6,748 of the M4 and 6,281 of the M4A1, according to R. P. Hunnicutt.

perguntas.p: Why did the Sherman catch fire?
perguntas.r: Mainly because of the ammunition stowed in the hull sides, not the gasoline. In an American study of 1945, 60% to 80% of the first Shermans burned when penetrated; with the ammunition in liquid-filled bins, 10% to 15%.

perguntas.p: Did the FEB have Sherman tanks?
perguntas.r: It had no tanks of its own. According to the magazine of the Armor Instruction Center, the only Brazilian unit to use armor in the war was the reconnaissance squadron, with M8 cars. The medium tanks at Montese were American.

perguntas.p: Where did the Sherman first see combat?
perguntas.r: At the second battle of El Alamein, in Egypt, in October 1942, with the British 8th Army, which had 252 of them ready.
